profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer - AWS Edge products and Amazon Linux / KaOS
profile.summary: Want to work at the interface between engineering imagination and the materialized network? Do you enjoy working on cellular, fault tolerant, micro service architectures? Come help us build the command and control system for AWS’s next generation network and redefine networking. Please reach out to find out more.

patents.title: Dependent network resources
patents.description: In certain aspects, where a network resource is configured (e.g., created, launched, modified, etc.) the dependencies between the network resource and other resources can be determined and stored. Subsequently, then a request is made to reconfigure the network resource, the stored dependencies can be accessed to determine whether or not to allow such a requested reconfiguration.

patents.title: COMPILING FIREWALL RULES INTO EXECUTABLE PROGRAMS
patents.description: This patent relates to a service provider network (e.g., AWS) to compile firewall rules into executable programs, such as eBPF programs, that are executable by a packet-processing device to evaluate packets in data flows. Traditionally, firewall rules (such as security groups for VPCs) are implemented as groups of C code snippets that describe properties of data packets, such as destination ports and CIDR blocks, that are allowed to pass through the firewall. However, the execution of these traditional firewall rules is slow, computationally inefficient, can include the execution of extraneous branches, and suffers from other inefficiencies. The process of compiling the C code into eBPF code optimizes the firewall rules (e.g., removing extraneous branches), and the execution of eBPF code is faster and more computationally efficient compared to executing the C code (e.g., less data fetching in memory). By converting firewall rules into eBPF code (or similar data structures), packet-processing devices can evaluate packets against firewall rules more efficiently.
